result.cause:
This is a known, still-open WebKit regression that started in iOS 26. It matches the user's report almost exactly. The tracker entry is WebKit bug 301108, "REGRESSION (iOS 26): <meta name=viewport> does not work correctly for viewport-fit=cover or height=device-height". It is status NEW, rdar://163501215, and none of the comments describe a fix.

The bug: an app added to the Home Screen with apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style=black-translucent and viewport-fit=cover is drawn from the very top of the screen, but WebKit makes its layout viewport shorter than the screen by exactly env(safe-area-inset-top). Measured cases:
- iPhone 17 Pro: screen 874, innerHeight 812, top inset 62. Seen in Web Inspector on a fresh install (jessemorley/Invoice#109) and in the iOS 26.2 simulator (zarda#493, frappe-ui#1284/#1289).
- A real iPhone on iOS 26.6.1: screen.height 844, innerHeight, visualViewport.height, 100vh, 100dvh and html/body/#root all 797, a 47 shortfall (busssss#23).
- An 852pt screen: about 793 (ferretry#668).
- A 926pt screen: page ends at 879 (trailhead#126).
- This device (iPhone 15 Pro Max, 932 screen, 59 status bar): the same rule predicts innerHeight 873.

The arithmetic matches the screenshot. Stage measure() takes H=873 and k=430/390=1.1026, so content = (873-59-34)/1.1026 = 707 frame px. That is below 730, so the layout switches to fit-tight and the logo goes to one row. The tab bar ends about 873 and the bottom ~59pt is empty. With the correct H=932, content would be 761 and the fit would be "normal". Chromium can't reproduce the bug (frappe-ui, ferretry and horde-run all say so), which is why emulation looks fine.

Why it happens and stays: frappe-ui's simulator work (PR #1284/#1289, also gameplan#608 and Safe-Sips#17) found that WebKit keeps the short viewport only while the document is no taller than that short viewport. When the page is at least screen-tall, iOS gives it the full viewport. zarda#493 shows the same thing from the other side: a downward drag fixes it (812 -> 874), and closing the keyboard after a low field brings it back.

This app is exactly the case that never recovers:
- html, body {height:100%} is set in both index.html and styles.css, so the document is always exactly as tall as the short viewport.
- body has overflow:hidden and overscroll-behavior:none, so the user can never drag the document and trigger the expansion.
- #root is position:fixed; inset:0 and .viewport is absolute inset:0, so root.clientHeight follows the short fixed containing block.
- The app has text inputs (src/ui/Leaderboard.tsx username, src/ui/Search.tsx). On a Pro Max, closing the keyboard has been reported to shrink innerHeight, visualViewport.height and 100dvh from 932 to 873 (dev.to article, iOS 17/18) or to re-shorten the viewport (zarda#493). So the gap can come back mid-session even when launch is fine.

What it is not: Safari 26.1's note "Fixed a bottom gap appearing on layouts with viewport-sized fixed containers on iOS (158055568)" covers the Safari-tab and keyboard case (Apple forums 799216 and 803987). Standalone reports from 26.2 (simulator), 26.5 and 26.6.1 (real device) show the Home Screen bug is still there.

iOS 27 is unclear. One iOS 27 report (meshmonitor#5310) saw a plain fixed bottom:0 bar reach the real bottom. It read innerHeight 956 against documentElement.clientHeight 894, so the inconsistency may now be in clientHeight. That report did not confirm a cause. The user's iOS version is unknown.
result.whatMeasuresWrong:
WRONG (short by the top inset, e.g. 873 instead of 932 on this phone) in iOS 26 standalone with black-translucent and viewport-fit=cover:
- window.innerHeight (812/874 in Web Inspector and the 26.2 simulator; 797/844 on a 26.6.1 device).
- visualViewport.height (797 on device; ~793/852 in ferretry).
- document.documentElement.clientHeight and html/body/#root heights (797 on device). This also applies to any element sized height:100% from html/body, so .viewport/#root clientHeight, which Stage.measure() reads first, is short too.
- 100dvh and 100svh. Equal to the short 812 in zarda#493; dvh measured 797 on device.
- position:fixed; inset:0 / bottom:0. The fixed containing block stops at the short edge (frappe-ui, hekate, zarda, busssss).
- 100vh is unreliable. It was 797 (wrong) on the 26.6.1 device. Older advice from WebKit 254868 (iOS 16-18) and the fozzedout gist says vh includes the inset in standalone, so this changed by version. Don't rely on it.

Painting is limited too, not just measurement. Making a fixed or in-flow element taller than the short viewport does NOT draw into the strip:
- frappe-ui#1284: a 100lvh shell was laid out to 874 but drawn only to 812, cutting off the tab bar labels.
- busssss#23: a min-height:891 box grew, but painting still stopped at 797, and a bottom:-47px bleed layer never painted.
- jessemorley#109: a fixed element in the strip never paints.
So setting the frame height from screen.height in JS on its own would clip the bottom 59pt of the tab bar.

TRUSTWORTHY:
- screen.height: 932/874/844/926 in every report. In landscape, read screen.width/height as the portrait dimensions.
- env(safe-area-inset-top) and env(safe-area-inset-bottom): 59/34 here, 62/34 and 47/34 elsewhere. The gap equals the top inset, which is useful for detection.
- 100lvh: 874 = full screen at cold launch in the zarda simulator table; it is the basis of the frappe-ui fix. Caveat: WebKit 316008 says 100vh and lvh are also wrong (full-screen, page scrolls) when the app was installed WITHOUT black-translucent, so lvh must be capped.

Self-check on device: screen.height - innerHeight == env(safe-area-inset-top) (59) with no keyboard open means the bug is present.

fixes.tradeoffs:
Evidence is from the simulator only. None of the sources I read confirms it on a physical iPhone, so it needs a check on the user's 15 Pro Max after deploy.

One app-specific unknown: body here has overflow:hidden, which propagates to the viewport, plus overscroll-behavior:none. The frappe and gameplan apps scroll normally, and no source says whether the 'document taller than viewport' heuristic still fires when the viewport can't scroll. If it doesn't, try moving overflow:hidden off body and onto #root/.viewport (already overflow:hidden), so the document stays non-scrollable in practice.

The min() cap is what keeps opaque-status-bar installs (top inset 0) from scrolling by the status-bar height (WebKit 316008); plain 100lvh would break them. Browser tabs and Android are unaffected because of the display-mode query. Landscape and keyboard behaviour were not checked by frappe. zarda#493 says a 100lvh floor also keeps the nav on the edge after the keyboard closes, and lists that as an acceptance check.

fixes.fix: Re-measure and self-heal after the keyboard and lifecycle events. In Stage, also call update() on focusout/blur of inputs (after ~150-350ms), pageshow and visibilitychange. If screen.height - innerHeight still about equals the top inset with no input focused, force a reflow: toggle display:none and back on the full-height root and read offsetHeight in between (dev.to cederhook technique; the fozzedout gist also suggests toggling viewport-fit to auto and back on cold start).
fixes.tradeoffs: This is a workaround, not a cure, and it can flicker; the dev.to author covers the flicker with a blurred overlay. It is only needed if the gap comes back after typing a username or using search with fix 1 in place. It reportedly doesn't help in a Safari tab. It costs little because Stage already listens to resize and visualViewport resize.

fixes.fix: Defensive detection in measure() and a diagnostic overlay, used together with fix 1, not instead of it. In iOS standalone (navigator.standalone or matchMedia('(display-mode: standalone)')), measure a hidden probe with height:100lvh and compare innerHeight/clientHeight against screen.height and the probe. Several projects added such a readout so device reports carry numbers: ferretry 'Viewport details', orbit menu readout, band, meshmonitor ?vpdebug=1. Include screen.height, innerHeight, documentElement.clientHeight, visualViewport.height, the #root rect, 100vh/dvh/svh/lvh probe heights, env() insets, display-mode and the UA iOS version. Optionally, when the bug is detected, choose the fit class from the screen-derived height.
fixes.tradeoffs: Do NOT just size the stage from screen.height and translate the tab bar into the strip; trailhead#126 did this with a --screen-gap variable, unverified. frappe-ui#1284 and busssss#23 show WebKit doesn't paint (and maybe doesn't deliver taps) below the short edge, so the bottom of the tab bar gets clipped. The overlay itself is cheap and settles which value is wrong on the user's actual iOS version, which matters because iOS 27 may behave differently (meshmonitor#5310).

fixes.fix: Fallback: switch apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style from black-translucent to opaque 'black' (or 'default'). iOS then starts the web view below the status bar and gives it the full remaining height to the real bottom. busssss#23 saw y=47..844 with 'default'. jessemorley/Invoice#109 confirmed it on a fresh install with Web Inspector (screen 874, innerHeight 812 before), and orbit#754 and band#681 shipped it.
fixes.tradeoffs: This loses the full-bleed top: the top 59pt becomes an opaque system bar that CSS can't paint. That is visually minor for this dark #04121a game, and Stage would just see sat=0. Big catch: iOS reads the apple-mobile-web-app-* tags only at install time (WebKit 316008, orbit#754, band#681/#697, jessemorley#109). The user and every existing install would have to delete and re-add the app; band added an in-app 'please re-install' notice for this. Without black-translucent, WebKit 316008 says 100vh/100lvh report the full screen and the page can scroll, so any lvh-based rule must keep the min() cap. Also update the launch-image and theme-color expectations.

busssss#23 found the shortfall just moves to the top edge. env(safe-area-inset-*) then reads 0 (fozzedout gist), which breaks the --sat/--sab inset handling and the landscape rotation logic in stage.tsx.

result.affected:
iOS 26.0 through at least 26.6.1, and possibly iOS 27.

Reproduced in:
- the iOS 26.2 simulator (frappe-ui, zarda)
- a real device on iOS 26.5 (very-happy#479)
- a real device on iOS 26.6.1 (busssss#23)
- fresh iOS 26 installs (jessemorley#109)

Not fixed by Safari 26.1's bottom-gap fix (158055568), which targets Safari tabs and the keyboard. WebKit 301108 is still NEW.

On iOS 27 (current), the one report I read (meshmonitor#5310) gives a mixed picture and does not confirm the same bug.

Trigger conditions:
- Home Screen / standalone mode (display:standalone in the manifest, apple-mobile-web-app-capable=yes) AND
- apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style=black-translucent (as stored at install time) AND
- viewport-fit=cover AND
- the document is no taller than the short viewport (e.g. html, body {height:100%} with no document scroll).

The gap re-appears after the soft keyboard closes. This was seen on iOS 17/18 in the dev.to report (932 -> 873 on a Pro Max) and in the iOS 26.2 simulator (zarda#493).

Not affected:
- Safari tabs, which have their own separate toolbar issues
- Android
- Chromium emulation
- installs with an opaque status bar, which have a different bug (WebKit 316008: vh/lvh too tall)

Older, related standalone and viewport-fit=cover height bug: WebKit 254868 (iOS 16 to 18.3.1, svh/visualViewport exclude the inset).

result.diagnosis:
I could not test on a real device. Everything below comes from reading the code and checking the numbers against the screenshot.

**Where the height comes from**
- `measure()` (src/stage.tsx:76-77) gets the window size from `VH = root.clientHeight || window.innerHeight`.
- `root` is the `.viewport` element. In CSS it is `position:absolute; inset:0` inside `#root`, which is `position:fixed; inset:0` (styles.css:61-71).
- So `VH` is the height of iOS's layout viewport, the box that fixed elements are sized against.
- Because `clientHeight` is never 0, `window.innerHeight` is never read. `screen.height` and `navigator.standalone` are never looked at.
- The insets come from a separate source: `.inset-probe` reads its padding, which is set to `env(safe-area-inset-*)`. That value is correct on the device (top 59, bottom 34). This is why the top bar lands in the right place.

**What happens on the iPhone**
- The app runs from the home screen (standalone mode) with the `black-translucent` status bar and `viewport-fit=cover`.
- In that mode iOS sometimes sizes the layout viewport as if the status bar were solid: screen height minus the status bar, 932 - 59 = 873pt. It still draws the page from the very top of the screen, under the status bar. This is a known kind of WebKit bug in home-screen web apps; I can't confirm which iOS releases have it.
- `measure()` trusts that 873:
  - H = 873, scale k = 430/390 = 1.1026
  - frame height h = H/k = 791.8 frame px, so it ends at 873pt
  - content height = (873 - 59 - 34)/k = 707.4, which is under 730, so the screen gets the `fit-tight` class
  - `.fit-tight .logo` (styles.css:716) is the one-row logo the user saw
- The fixed `#root` and `.viewport` are also only 873pt tall, so `.viewport`'s `overflow:hidden` would cut off anything taller anyway.
- Below 873 you see the html/body background (#04121a). That is the ~60pt empty strip. The tab bar really ends at about 873pt, which matches the ~870pt measured.
- Nothing is actually pushed up. The top is correct and the frame is 59pt too short.

**Expected with the fix**
- With H = 932: content = 761.0 (`fit-normal`), the frame bottom is at 932pt, and the splash is centred at 466pt, the same as the launch image (now 436.5pt, so it jumps about 30pt at launch).

**Why emulation looks correct**
- The device test script in this session's scratchpad (`devices.js`, profile `pm-app`) creates a Chromium viewport of 430x932 and passes the insets in through `__psInsets`.
- In Chromium the layout viewport, `innerHeight` and `screen` are all 932, and `navigator.standalone` does not exist. So it tests the ideal iOS behaviour and cannot show this bug.

**Is the strip inside the web view?**
- Probably yes, so the page can draw there. The strip shows page background, and WKWebView normally draws content past its layout viewport (Safari tabs draw under their translucent bars).
- This is not proven: `theme-color`, the manifest `background_color` and the html background are all #04121a, so the screenshot can't tell them apart. A one-off device check: set `html{background:red}`. If the strip turns red, it is inside the web view.
evidence: src/stage.tsx:76-77: `const VW = root.clientWidth || window.innerWidth; const VH = root.clientHeight || window.innerHeight;`. `root` is `.viewport`, so the size is the fixed `#root` box (the layout viewport). `innerHeight` is never used while `clientHeight` is above 0, and `screen` and `navigator.standalone` are never checked.

src/styles.css:61-71: `#root{position:fixed;inset:0}` and `.viewport{position:absolute;inset:0;overflow:hidden}`. Even if the frame were sized correctly, `.viewport` would cut it off at the layout viewport height (873 on the device).
src/styles.css:76-85: `.inset-probe` is fixed and 0x0, with padding set to `env(safe-area-inset-*)`. It provides only the insets, which are correct on the device (top bar at ~65pt = 59 + padding).

Numbers: with H=873, k=1.1026, frame h=791.8, content=707.4, so `fit-tight` (under 730) and `.fit-tight .logo` one-row (styles.css:716), with the frame bottom at 873pt. This matches the ~870pt tab-bar bottom and the 59pt strip. With H=932, content=761.0 (`fit-normal`) and the bottom is at 932pt.

The content can only be under 730 if the top inset is about 59. With t=0 and H=873 it would be 761 (normal). So the frame starts at the top of the screen under the status bar and is 59pt short at the bottom. It is not shifted.
src/stage.tsx:166-167: the ResizeObserver watches `.viewport` (root). If `.viewport` gets an explicit size it will stop reporting changes, so the observer has to watch something else.

`devices.js` in this session's scratchpad (`pm-app`, around line 14 and line 204) emulates a 430x932 viewport with insets injected. Chromium's layout viewport and screen are both 932 and `navigator.standalone` is undefined, so the bug can't appear there.

src/styles.css:3437-3446: the splash says it matches the launch image. Centred in an 873pt frame it sits at 436.5pt instead of 466pt, so it jumps about 30pt when launched from the home screen. The same fix corrects this.

index.html, the manifest (`display:standalone`) and `theme-color` all use #04121a, the same as the html/body background. So the strip's colour can't prove whether it is page-drawn, but it fits WKWebView drawing past a short layout viewport.
risks: The fix assumes WKWebView covers the whole screen and only reports a short layout viewport, so it can draw in the 873-932 strip. If some iOS release makes the web view itself short, the corrected frame would put the bottom ~59pt of the tab bar off-screen, which is worse than today. Check on the device: with the fix the tab bar should reach the bottom. A one-off `html{background:red}` test also shows whether the strip is part of the page.

Taps in the 873-932 strip land outside iOS's reported layout viewport. WebKit should still hit-test the overflowing fixed content there, but check on the device by tapping the lower half of each tab button (the tab bar is about 830-932pt tall).

If WebKit ever clipped a fixed element's overflow at the layout viewport, `.viewport` would draw but be cut at 873. The fallback is to size `#root` the same way: set a `--app-h` variable on `documentElement` from `measure()` and use `#root{bottom:auto;height:var(--app-h,100%)}`. The probe stays `inset:0`, so there is still no feedback loop.

The shortfall limit of 80 or less is a heuristic. It covers every iPhone status bar (20-62pt) and leaves out keyboards (216pt and up). A real status-bar-sized shrink in a full-width standalone iPhone app, such as the old double-height in-call bar that iOS 13+ no longer has, would be wrongly treated as the bug. To tighten it, require `Math.abs((sh - h) - t) <= 4`, where `t` is the probe's top inset.

The ResizeObserver now watches the probe instead of `.viewport`. Anything else that relied on `.viewport`'s inset:0 size, such as the `.viewport.wide` background in framed mode, keeps working because its inline size equals the window size. Run the full device matrix (Safari tab, Android, iPad framed, both sideways directions) to confirm nothing changed outside iOS standalone portrait.
otherLayoutRisks: Late safe-area insets: today the ResizeObserver watches `.viewport`, which does not change size when only the `env()` insets change. If iOS reports insets of 0 for the first frames after launch or resume and no resize event follows, `--sat`/`--sab` stay 0 and the top bar sits under the Dynamic Island. Watching the probe's content box (part of the fix) and re-measuring on `pageshow`/`visibilitychange` covers this.

Keyboard: the NameSheet field has `autoFocus` and there is a room-code input in Search.tsx. When an input is focused, iOS scrolls the visual viewport or document to show it, even with `body{overflow:hidden}` and a fixed `#root`. The whole app then moves up under the status bar. Some iOS 26 builds have left that offset in place after the keyboard closes, which would look exactly like 'pushed up into the top bar'. Mitigation: on `focusout`, and when `visualViewport.height` returns to full, call `window.scrollTo(0,0)`. Also consider not auto-focusing on first launch.

Safari tabs on iOS 26 (floating Liquid Glass toolbar, with compact, bottom and top tab layouts): the fixed box may or may not reach behind the floating toolbar, and `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` varies between layouts. The tab bar could end up partly behind Safari's toolbar or leave a gap above it. Test all three Safari tab layouts and landscape, where the bars hide.

Rotation timing: iOS sends new sizes and `screen.orientation.angle` late. The single 350ms retry can still read stale values on a slow device, giving a frame turned the wrong way or with the old size until the next event. Watching the probe makes the update event-driven. A second retry around 800ms would be cheap insurance.
Sideways phone: the 21pt home-indicator inset becomes one side of the counter-rotated frame. The 16px gutter is about 17.6pt at k≈1.1, so content can come about 3pt into the home-indicator strip.

iPad home-screen app in Split View, Slide Over or Stage Manager: the window is not the screen. The fix only acts when the screen's short side is 600 or less and the window spans the full screen width, so the iPad is never corrected. Never use `screen` sizes on iPad.

Other iPhones: the 16 Pro and Pro Max have a 62pt island inset, and Display Zoom reports smaller screen sizes (for example 375x812). All sizes come from `env()`, the probe and `screen`, so they adapt. Models without a matching `apple-touch-startup-image` only see a launch flash, not a layout problem.

Future iOS changes: if Apple fixes the bug, the shortfall becomes 0 and the correction does nothing. If the bug changes form (for example a short width, or a shortfall in landscape), it won't be corrected. Keep the emulated 'iOS standalone short viewport' profile in the device matrix and check on a real device after each iOS update.

result.cause:
This is almost certainly the iOS 26+ (also seen on iOS 27) home-screen-app short viewport, WebKit bug 301108 (rdar 163501215, still NEW and unfixed). In standalone mode with viewport-fit=cover and apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style=black-translucent, WebKit lays the page out one status bar shorter than the screen whenever the document is shorter than the screen. On a 15 Pro Max that is 932 - 59 = 873. Fixed content is not painted below that edge, and iOS fills the band with the page background colour.

The numbers match the report exactly:
- The app sizes the frame from root.clientHeight, and the root sits inside #root {position:fixed; inset:0}, so it gets 873.
- With k = 430/390, the frame is h = 791.8 tall. Content = 791.8 - 53.5 - 30.8 = 707.4 frame px. That is under 730, so fit becomes 'tight' and the logo switches to the one-row layout. With 932 the content would be 761 ('normal').
- The tab bar ends at 873, which matches the ~870 seen in the screenshot.
- Chromium emulation cannot reproduce it. Every source says so. The Xcode iOS 26.2 simulator does reproduce it.

What brings the full viewport back:
- Dragging the page (zarda/home-account #493).
- Making the document at least as tall as the screen (frappe-ui #1289; raven #66 saw innerHeight go from 793 to 852 on an installed iPhone).

What makes it short again: closing a keyboard that had scrolled the page.

A second cause gives the same number. On iOS 17 and 18, the first software-keyboard open in a standalone PWA shrinks innerHeight, visualViewport.height and 100dvh from 932 to 873 on a Pro Max, and they stay there until a force-quit (dev.to/cederhook). This app has text inputs (the leaderboard username and Search). If the gap is already there on a cold launch before any typing, it is 301108 rather than the keyboard bug.

Some fixes do not apply here:
- Safari 26.1 fixed "a bottom gap appearing on layouts with viewport-sized fixed containers on iOS" (158055568), but that is a different Safari-tab bug. Reports from iOS 26.2 to 26.6 and from iOS 27 show the standalone shortfall is still there.
- WebKit bug 301994 (status bar opaque again, top inset 0) is a separate regression. It was fixed in 26.2, then reopened for 26.5.2 and the iOS 27 beta. It is not this symptom, because here the top is correct.
result.whatMeasuresWrong:
State: iOS 26.x/27, home-screen app, black-translucent + viewport-fit=cover, page not taller than the screen. Values are for the iPhone 15 Pro Max (430x932, insets 59/34).

Wrong (short by the top inset, i.e. 873):
- window.innerHeight. One iOS 27 report (meshmonitor #5310) had innerHeight correct at 956 while documentElement.clientHeight was short at 894, so don't trust innerHeight alone.
- document.documentElement.clientHeight.
- visualViewport.height (offsetTop 0).
- height:100% on html/body/#root.
- Any position:fixed element with inset:0 or bottom:0. This is the app's root.clientHeight. Fixed content is also clipped at this edge: frappe-ui found a 100lvh-tall fixed shell still stopped at 812 of 874, and the busssss PR found screen.height-based JS heights, hard-coded px heights and bottom:-47px bleed layers all stopped at 797 of 844. Apple forum 800798 reports the same iOS 26 clipping of fixed content.
- 100dvh.
- 100svh. With black-translucent it is short; with the default status bar the values flip (sokosumi #4666).
- -webkit-fill-available. WebKit 254868 says svh, -webkit-fill-available and visualViewport.height subtract the insets in standalone with cover; still reproducible on iOS 18.3.1.

Right:
- 100vh and 100lvh resolve to the full screen (932) in standalone with black-translucent (WebKit 301994 comment 6, Brawnet #25, home-account #493). They overstate the viewport when the status bar is opaque (WebKit 316008), which is why fixes cap them with min(..., 100% + top inset).
- screen.height = 932. iOS reports it for the portrait screen, so take max(screen.width, screen.height) and only use it when upright. It gives the target height, not the painted height.
- env(safe-area-inset-top/bottom) = 59/34.

iOS 17/18 (no 301108):
- At cold start in standalone, 100vh, innerHeight and screen.height agree at 932.
- 100dvh can be wrong on cold start until a portrait-landscape-portrait rotation (fozzedout gist).
- After the first keyboard, innerHeight, visualViewport.height and 100dvh drop to 873 and stay there (dev.to).

How the values change over time:
- Cold launch: short.
- Once the page is screen-tall: the full value arrives within about 170 ms (iOS 26.2 simulator, home-account #494). A drag also restores it.
- Keyboard open and close: short again without the floor, still full with it.
- Backgrounded for hours (iOS 17): fixed bottom bars shift up as if a phantom toolbar were present. Unresolved, Apple forum 744327.
- Rotation: sizes are stale for several resize events, 500 ms or more on iOS 17+. Rotating to landscape and back can clear the gap.

Conclusion: the app's measurement (the fixed root's clientHeight) is the true painted height. The fix is to make WebKit enlarge the viewport, not to substitute screen.height. A frame sized to 932 while the viewport is still 873 would have its tab bar cut off.

fixes.tradeoffs:
It relies on undocumented WebKit behaviour (a page at least screen-tall gets the full viewport). Evidence is mostly the iOS 26.2 simulator plus one installed-iPhone report (raven); there is no Apple statement.
It does nothing on iOS 17/18, Android, desktop, Safari tabs and opaque status bars: there the min() resolves to 100%, so nothing scrolls. It also stays harmless if Apple fixes the bug.
The first frame can still be short (it settled within ~170 ms in the simulator), so the JS must re-measure. The existing ResizeObserver, resize and visualViewport listeners cover that.

If the viewport does not grow, the document can scroll by up to 59 px. A drag at that point is exactly what makes iOS hand over the full height, and overscroll-behavior:none stops the bounce. Once the viewport is full, html = screen = viewport and nothing scrolls.
Whether the floor works with body overflow:hidden still in place is unverified, so test both on a device.

Never size the frame from screen.height or 100lvh while short is true. WebKit clips fixed content at the short edge, so the tab bar would be cut off: frappe saw labels clipped when layout reached 874 but painting stopped at 812.
The WIP fitDocument() sets an html min-height in px equal to screen.height. That does not depend on 100lvh and is fine, but it must stay cleared when sideways, as the WIP already does.

It can flash for one frame; the article covers it with a short blurred veil. The timings were tuned by hand.
The WIP heal uses window.scrollTo(0,1). The article lists scrollTo as not working for the keyboard case, though home-account found that a real drag does fix the 301108 state. Consider using the display toggle as the fallback.

findings.title: Legend bot's 'deny' scan only looks at a cell's top 12 players, which in football often leaves out the DEF or the TE
findings.scenario: yourBestGain() checks only CELL_BY_ID[cellId].players.slice(0, 12). A football cell has about 30 players (an NBA cell about 79) sorted by value, and position caps make a single slot matter. In 32 of 183 NFL cells the only DEF ranks below 12th, and in 8 cells every TE does. Example: you hold QB/RB/WR/TE/FLEX and only DEF is open, and the Legend bot picks first in a cell whose defense ranks 13th or lower. Then base = deny = 0, so Legend ignores what each pick would take from you. I ran a probe over 2000 partial lineups against random cells. The 12-player scan underestimates your best gain by more than 0.5 rating points in 3.1% of NFL cases, against 0.1% in NBA, and reads 0 when a real gain exists in 23 NFL cases against 1 NBA case. Legend plays noticeably weaker denial in football. NBA is effectively unaffected.
findings.fix: Scan every player for football only, so basketball's bot choices stay the same: `const scan = NFL ? CELL_BY_ID[cellId].players : CELL_BY_ID[cellId].players.slice(0, 12)`. A cheaper option is to scan the top 12 plus the best player at each open slot.

findings.title: NFL win curve's 16.5-win anchor makes 17-win playoff opponents about 11 rating points stronger than 16-win ones, and stronger than most 17-0 user teams
findings.scenario: winsFromRating rounds 16.5 up, so a user team goes 17-0 from rating 139.5. But ratingForWins(17) returns 143, the last anchor, while ratingForWins(16) is 132.2. The 1972 Dolphins and the 2007 Patriots (w17 = 17, both in the Super Bowl pool) are rated 143. Every 17-0 user team rated 139.5 to 143 (nearly all of them; 143 is the simulated maximum) is an underdog to those teams on neutral ground: 43% at 139.5. A 16-1 team gets only 30% against them, versus 50% against a 16-win opponent. This also pulls the real title odds of a minimal 17-0 team down to about 63%, against the documented ~70%. nfl.test.ts doesn't catch this because it tests at ratingForWins(17)+2 = 145, a rating above the simulated maximum.
findings.fix: Rate a 17-win opponent at the least rating that earns 17 wins, as basketball does (its 82-win anchor 109.1 is within 0.3 of where 82 starts): replace the [139.5,16.5],[143,17] pair with [139.5,17]. Then recalibrate or recheck the 0.15% / 70% figures, or special-case ratingForWins(17) = 139.5 for NFL. Also run the 17-0 test at the real minimum 17-0 rating.

findings.title: Trade cannot swap your defense for the same franchise's defense from another decade (DEF pid 'D-<franchise>' counts as a duplicate)
findings.scenario: Classic mode: you hold 'Cardinals Defense' from ARI-1970 at DEF, spin ARI-2010 and arm Trade to upgrade. whyUnavailable sees the same pid 'D-ARI' in your lineup and returns 'dup', so the better Cardinals Defense is greyed out. There is only one DEF slot, so the trade could only replace the unit you hold, never hold it twice; the code comment says the rule exists to stop that. For players the same rule still matters, because a traded-in Walter Payton could take FLEX while his other decade stays at RB. For defenses it only blocks a legitimate upgrade. NBA has the same check for one person across two decades, so any change must be limited to football.
findings.fix: Only when NFL and s.armed === 'trade': allow the duplicate when every slot holding that pid is one the new player can fill and the trade replaces it. For DEF: `if (NFL && s.armed === 'trade' && p.pos[0] === 'DEF') skip the dup check`, since the trade can only target the DEF slot. eligibleSlots already limits it to DEF.

findings.title: 76 NFL Prime targets point to a team-decade the player was cut from, so Prime does nothing for them (4 lose a real upgrade)
findings.scenario: The build script chooses each player's prime cell from all his lines with 8+ games, and only afterwards applies POS_CAP to each cell's list. When the prime cell's capped list drops him, primeVersion() finds no player there and returns null. Examples: Rex Burkhead CIN-2010 (val 3.0) points to NE-2010, where he isn't listed, though NE-2020 lists him at 8.7. Joey Harrington DET-2000 (10.9) points to MIA-2000, which doesn't list him, though ATL-2000 lists him at 11.2. Prime shows him as not upgradable. NBA data has 0 such refs.
findings.fix: Choose the prime cell from the lines that survive POS_CAP: build the `keep` lists first, then compute `prime` over kept entries only. Rebuild nfl.json; this changes the NFL DATA_V only, not NBA's '1gypzor'.

findings.title: After a "didn't connect" timeout the host drops out of the private room and lands in the public queue, while the friend keeps waiting in the room
findings.scenario: Host creates code K7QM in Search (that room lives only in Search's own state; App's roomCode stays null). The friend opens the invite link, or taps SWITCH TO NFL from the room notice, so the friend's App roomCode is K7QM. They pair, but the guest misses every 'go' and the host's first match messages. After 12 s the host's onFound timer runs setScreen('search'). Search remounts with room={roomCode}=null, so the host is on the QUICK MATCH tab in the public queue and gets the AI after 30 s. The guest remounts back in 'Joining K7QM…' and waits forever. The same stale roomCode also hurts link and SWITCH joiners later: one who cancels the room, pairs in Quick Match and then hits the timeout is sent back into the old friend room, not the queue. This was already there before the NFL commit, but the new SWITCH reload path relies on roomCode, so more friend matches now take this path.
findings.fix: Have App track the room Search is actually in, as {code, hosting}. Search reports it through an onRoom callback and initialises from it, hosting flag included. On the didn't-connect fallback, put the player back into that same room as host or joiner. Clear it when the player cancels or switches to Quick Match.

findings.title: Queued leaderboard entries and name changes for one sport are only sent while that sport is open; they can expire unsent
findings.scenario: (a) A player finishes a ranked NFL Daily or a Classic run on a weak connection, and Results says it is queued. They go Home and switch to NBA. flushLb only sends the open sport's profile.lb.dirty, so the NFL entry sits in 'perfect-season:profile:nfl:v1'. If they reopen NFL on a later day or week, prune() at mount drops the past Daily and weekly entries from entries and dirty, so they never reach those boards. (b) A player renames in NBA. NameSheet promises 'Your results on the boards switch to the new name', but NFL boards and the NFL H2H board keep the old name until NFL is opened again. That is never, for someone who stopped playing NFL.
findings.fix: lb.entries keys are full d-tags (they already include the sport's namespace), so either page can publish the other sport's entries. In profile.ts, add a helper that reads and updates the other sport's lb (rename it, list its dirty entries). Have flushLb and the rename paths in App also publish the other sport's dirty entries and clear them in that stored part.

findings.title: Switching sport reloads straight away and cuts off the 30-second post-match resend that app updates deliberately wait for
findings.scenario: A player finishes a Head to Head draft with their last pick. finish() runs endMatch(false, 30000), so MatchConn keeps re-sending the final state every 2.5 s, and lingerUntil records this. The applyUpdate effect waits until lingerUntil, because 'a reload would cut that short'. The player taps Home and then the NBA/NFL switch within those 30 s. goSport reloads after 420 ms and ignores lingerUntil, so the resends stop. If the stored copy from persist() did not reach a relay and the opponent's phone was briefly in the background, their phone goes silent for 20 s and the AI takes over this player's draft. The two phones then record different results (a real result here, 'they left' there).
findings.fix: In goSport, wait max(420, lingerUntil.current - Date.now()) ms before calling switchSport (keep the fade showing), or block the switch with a short toast until the linger ends.

findings.title: The shared online count makes 1 vs 1 show LIVE and 'N online' when the only other players are in the other sport and can never be matched
findings.scenario: One player has NBA open and one has NFL open. ONLINE_TAG ('ps1-online') is the same for both sports, so the NBA home screen shows '2 online' and a LIVE badge on 1 vs 1. Queues are split by NET_V, so the NBA player taps FIND A MATCH, sees 'No one else is searching yet' and gets the AI after 30 s. This changes NBA behaviour: before, everyone counted could be matched.
findings.fix: Add the sport to presence beats ({ name, st, sp: SPORT }) and count per-sport presence for the LIVE badge, or base `live` on the sport-specific searching count. The whole-app 'online' number can stay on the chip if wanted.

findings.title: The room mismatch notice never clears, so it keeps offering a switch (or saying the friend is switching) after the friend has left
findings.scenario: A host on NFL waits in room K7QM. A friend types K7QM on NBA. The host sees 'Joe joined from NBA. Their phone is offering to switch to NFL', and Joe sees SWITCH TO NFL. Joe taps Back instead. onLobby only ever sets the mismatch and nothing expires it (it is reset only when the search effect restarts), so the host's notice stays for as long as they wait. Same in reverse: if the host gives up, the joiner's SWITCH button stays, and tapping it reloads the app into the other sport with ?room=K7QM, a room nobody is in, and changes their saved sport.
findings.fix: Store the time the last lobby event was seen with the mismatch. Hide it after about 6 s without a new lobby event, matching the Matchmaker's fresh() window, for example via the existing 250 ms `now` tick in Search.

findings.title: Home-screen fix: the `body { overflow: visible }` rule never applies, so the page still can't scroll and the 59pt-short viewport isn't released
findings.scenario: Commit 96d5c0c says the fix depends on the body being able to scroll in home-screen mode, so that iOS hands over the full screen height ('a drag does it'). It adds `@media (display-mode: standalone) { body { overflow: visible; } }` at lines 46-55. Ten lines later the base `body { ... overflow: hidden; ... }` rule (lines 62-67) has the same specificity and comes later, so it wins in every mode; a media query adds no specificity. On an iPhone home-screen app in the short-viewport state (the iPhone 15 Pro Max case in the commit message), the root scroller stays overflow:hidden. A drag can never scroll it, so only the one-off programmatic scrollTo(0,1) nudge is left. The frame can stay a status bar short, the compact layout gets picked, and the 'doesn't fit the screen' symptom remains. The rule is dead code as written.
findings.fix: Put the standalone body override after the base body rule, or raise its specificity (e.g. `@media (display-mode: standalone) { html body { overflow: visible; } }`). Then confirm on a real iPhone home-screen app that the frame reaches the bottom edge and that dragging the page doesn't visibly move the fixed game.

findings.title: The whole iOS height fix is skipped when iOS reports a top safe-area inset of 0, which is how the matching iOS 26.1+/26.5/27 home-screen bug reports it
findings.scenario: fullScreenHeight() returns 0 when topInset < 20. shortfall() also needs |gap - topInset| <= 4. The CSS rule adds env(safe-area-inset-top) to 100%. All three only act when iOS reports the status-bar inset. The closest home-screen report, WebKit 301994 (iOS 26.1, still on 26.5.2 and iOS 27 beta), gives innerHeight 812 vs screen.height 874 and env(safe-area-inset-top) 0. The comments cite 301108, which is the Safari address-bar bug. In that state fitDocument clears min-height, heal() never runs, the CSS min-height equals 100%, and --sat stays 0. The frame keeps the short height with no top padding. If iOS draws the web layer from the top of the screen, the TopBar, draft header and Results top bar sit under the clock with an empty band at the bottom: the user's 'pushed up into the top bar'. The Settings viewportInfo() line shows view/doc/root/screen sizes but not the insets, so a report from the user's phone can't tell this case from the 59pt-inset case.
findings.fix: Add the probe's top and bottom insets to viewportInfo() and have the user read that line on the affected phone. Handle the standalone-portrait case where inset-top is 0 and screen.height - innerHeight is 20-64: apply the same min-height/heal path instead of bailing, and if the web view is confirmed to start at the screen top, use that gap as the top inset for --sat.

findings.title: NFL 17–0 season reveal pushes 'START THE PLAYOFFS' off the bottom on small screens
findings.scenario: Football swaps basketball's dot grid for 17 score tiles: 3 rows of 38px, 32px in compact, plus a 14px top margin. findings.title: First-launch Welcome screen shows basketball wording in football
findings.scenario: A new player opens a friend's NFL invite link (?room=K7QM&sport=nfl). SPORT becomes nfl, and with no name yet the first screen is Welcome. Its perks list says 'Draft five players from random NBA teams and decades'. The football draft has six rounds of NFL teams. This file was not touched by the NFL commit.

findings.title: Football YARDS / TDS sorts order by hidden totals while highlighting a single column, so the list looks mis-sorted
findings.scenario: sortValue('yds') is pass+rush+rec yards and sortValue('td') is pass+rush+rec TDs. hotFor() lights only PASS for a QB, only REC YDS for a WR/TE, and only the rushing TD for an RB, and the row never shows the total. Example, ARI 2020s sorted by YARDS: Kyler Murray (PASS 236, highlighted) is listed above Jacoby Brissett (PASS 240, highlighted). Same pair under TDS: Murray TD 1.4 above Brissett 1.6, and James Conner 0.6 above Kenyan Drake 0.7. Across the data there are 265 such same-position inversions for YARDS and 117 in the top 8 rows for TDS.
findings.fix: Sort by exactly the values that are highlighted: yds = passYds for QB, rushYds+recYds for RB, recYds for WR/TE; td = passTd for QB, rushTd for RB, recTd for WR/TE. Otherwise highlight every column that feeds the sum, including RUSH for QB/WR, and add a total column.

findings.title: Forced re-layout (#root display:none) replays every entrance animation and resets list scroll whenever the shortfall persists
findings.scenario: heal() flips #root to display:none and back if short() is still true 250ms after the scroll nudge. It runs again on every resume (onShow) and every keyboard close (onBlur resets healed). display:none restarts all CSS animations: rise-in rows, card-drop on the six field cards, logo letters, jumbo-in, view-up. It also resets scrollTop of every scroller inside. Scenario: iOS stays a status bar short (the case this path exists for). The player is scrolled down the Ranks board or Profile history, or the draft player list, and switches apps and comes back. 650ms later the list jumps to the top and everything on screen re-animates. This repeats on each return and after typing a name or room code.
findings.fix: Don't toggle display on #root. Force layout with a cheaper nudge (e.g. toggle a transform or height on .viewport, or re-run measure()). Or only do it once per launch, and save/restore scroll positions.

findings.title: Leaderboard lineup: the 'FLEX' slot label is wider than its 24px column and runs into the player's name
findings.scenario: Ranks, NFL, tap a board row to expand its lineup. .lbline i is an inline-block 24px wide at 12px weight 800, and the name follows it with no gap. Basketball slots (PG/SG/SF/PF/C) and QB/RB/WR/TE/DEF fit. 'FLEX' is about 28-30px, so its X overlaps the first letter of the FLEX player's name (e.g. 'FLEXKelce').

findings.title: Room-code mismatch banner pushes the bottom button off screen on the smallest phone
findings.scenario: On 375x548 Safari (compact, 570px frame) a friend's phone answers your room code from the other sport. The .mismatch box (~126px with its SWITCH button, ~76px for the host) is added inside .radar-wrap under the 170px radar, and nothing on the screen can shrink. Joining, the column is ~616px, so the CANCEL button shows only ~22 of its 56px. Hosting, it is ~644px and SEND INVITE / CANCEL is pushed fully below the edge.

result.reason:
The claim that Legend "plays noticeably weaker denial in football" does not hold up once you measure what Legend actually picks. The reviewer's probe measured how far the scanned `base` number is off. That is not the same as Legend picking a different player.

1. **Why the 12-player cut rarely matters.** In botPickFrom (src/engine/draft.ts), the deny term `0.6*(base - deny(p))` is only applied to the bot's own `top` list. That list is `cands.slice(0, 8)`: the bot's 8 most valuable players that fit its open slots. Cells are sorted by `val` (I checked all 183 NFL cells and 180 NBA cells). For one candidate p, `deny(p)` is lower than `base` only when p is your single best-gain player. So the 12-player cut can change a decision only when your best player ranks below 12th in the cell and is still in the bot's top 8. That needs at least 5 higher-ranked players who don't fit the bot's open slots. In the reviewer's example (you only need DEF), the cut matters only when the bot also needs DEF and that DEF is in its top 8. If DEF is the bot's only open slot, its pick is forced anyway.

2. **Measured effect.** I ran a script outside the repo with vite-node. It copies Legend's choice exactly, once with `slice(0, 12)` and once with a full scan, and compares them at every bot-first pick in 3000 simulated 1v1 Legend drafts per sport.
   - **You pick the best gain each round:** in NFL, 19 of 9000 Legend first picks change (0.21%). When they change, the full scan takes only 0.03 more rating points from your best remaining gain, on a team rating of about 100 to 140. In NBA, 6 of 7500 change (0.08%).
   - **You pick at random:** in NFL, 12 of 9000 change (0.13%), about 2 rating points each, under 0.3 wins. That is roughly 1 draft in 250. In NBA, 6 of 7500 change.

3. **Not new code.** The same `slice(0, 12)` heuristic was already in the parent commit 2a9a05c for NBA. It is a deliberate cost cap, not a football regression.

So there is no concrete failing path with a meaningful effect. Legend's denial in football is essentially the same either way, and nothing breaks.
result.betterFix: No change needed. If you want it exact, use the reviewer's cheaper option, for football only so basketball's bot choices stay the same: scan only the bot's own `top` candidates plus your best player at each open slot. Only those players can change the result. Or scan the full `players` list when NFL is set; about 30 players times about 8 candidates is cheap.
